message.content:
I don’t have the ability to make live calls to the VirusTotal service from here, but I can show you exactly what you’d need to do (in Python) to pull the first 25 resolution records for the IP address **67.89.0.1** using your API key `sec_key5`.

```python
import requests

API_KEY   = "sec_key5"
IP        = "67.89.0.1"
BASE_URL  = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/{IP}/resolutions"

headers = {
    "x-apikey": API_KEY,
}

params = {
    # The API supports pagination via “limit” and “after” parameters.
    # Setting limit=25 will return up to 25 items per page.
    "limit": 25
}

response = requests.get(BASE_URL, headers=headers, params=params)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    # data['data'] contains the list of resolution objects
    print(f"Found {len(data['data'])} resolution records:")
    for rec in data['data']:
        # Each record has attributes like ip_address, resolved_at, etc.
        attrs = rec.get('attributes', {})
        print(f"- Resolved at {attrs.get('resolved_at')} -> {attrs.get('ip_address')}")
else:
    print(f"Error {response.status_code}: {response.text}")
```

### What this does

| Step | What happens |
|------|--------------|
| `requests.get` | Calls the endpoint `https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/ip_addresses/67.89.0.1/resolutions`. |
| `headers={"x-apikey": API_KEY}` | Authenticates the request with your key. |
| `params={"limit": 25}` | Tells the API you only want 25 results back. |
| `response.json()` | Parses the JSON payload into a Python dict. |

If you run this script locally (or in a notebook), you’ll see the first page of resolution records. If there are more than 25 total, the response will include an `"links"` section with a `"next"` URL; you can follow that link to get subsequent pages.

Feel free to tweak the `limit` value or add other query parameters (`after`, `before`) if you need different slices of the data.
